**Benders decomposition** [@benders1962] splits a problem into a *master problem* over
the "complicating" variables and a *subproblem* that becomes an easy linear program once
those variables are fixed. The subproblem answers each proposal from the master with a
cut, and the two take turns until they agree. The method is the basis of the L-shaped
method in stochastic programming [@vanslyke1969] and was extended beyond linear
subproblems by @geoffrion1972.
